name.text: Greatest and least values on an interval

questiontext.text:
Find the greatest and least values of \(f(x) = {@f@}\) for \({@L1@} \le x \le {@U1@}\).

Greatest value: [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
Least value: [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
On an interval the greatest or least value may be at a stationary point or at an end. List the candidates, then compare.

\(f'(x) = {@df@} = {@3*a0*(x-p0)*(x-q0)@}\), so the stationary points are at \(x = {@p0@}\) and \(x = {@q0@}\), both inside the interval.

\(x\)\(f(x)\)Kind
\({@xs[1]@}\)\({@vs[1]@}\)end of the interval
\({@xs[2]@}\)\({@vs[2]@}\)stationary point
\({@xs[3]@}\)\({@vs[3]@}\)stationary point
\({@xs[4]@}\)\({@vs[4]@}\)end of the interval

The greatest value is \({@G@}\), at \(x = {@gx@}\). The least value is \({@Lv@}\), at \(x = {@lx@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Differentiation II: greatest and least values on an interval

Grade 12 CBE Core 4.1: Find the greatest and least values of a cubic on a closed interval by comparing the stationary values with the values at the ends.

Core

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: That is \(f\) at \(x = {@g2x@}\)[[if test="is(g2loc=1)"]], the maximum point,[[/if]] but \(f\) is larger elsewhere on the interval. Compare \(f\) at both stationary points and at both ends, \(x = {@L1@}\) and \(x = {@U1@}\).
That is the value of \(x\). Give the value of \(f\) there.

falsefeedback.text: List the candidates: the stationary points inside the interval and both ends. Work out \(f\) at each and choose the largest.

truefeedback.text: That is \(f\) at \(x = {@l2x@}\)[[if test="is(l2loc=1)"]], the minimum point,[[/if]] but \(f\) is smaller elsewhere on the interval. Compare \(f\) at both stationary points and at both ends, \(x = {@L1@}\) and \(x = {@U1@}\).
That is the value of \(x\). Give the value of \(f\) there.

falsefeedback.text: List the candidates: the stationary points inside the interval and both ends. Work out \(f\) at each and choose the smallest.
